AFTER CAUGHT IN INDIAN REVOLT, After having lived for several months under siege conditions in Peshawar?Northwest Frontier Province, of India, the only African gir, s in the Indian city--Lillian, Frieda and Eleanor Becker, and their parents of Harrison, N.Y. have just arrived at San Francisco from Calcutta, India. Two years of traveling throut northern China, Mongolia, Thibet and upper India, culminated in thrilling experiences at Pesahwar, where the girls were fired on by sniping hillmen, narrowly escaping bombin in a native raid on the bazaars, and lived for three months behind barbed wire entanglements and machine gun protections. One of the girls was captured at one time by the bandits but quick action by her brothers saved her. When the party came to leave Pesahwar, they were warned by British authorities that the first stage of their journey might prove hazardous if made in European clothing.
